p: The video starts with a generated spec file and asks 'Who reviews it?'. It displays a shared URL doc where text is selected and a comment 'Give me the 3-week cut' is added. A terminal executes a Claude CLI command applying the comments, after which the live document metrics update smoothly on the same URL. It finishes with an Artifact Share branded CTA screen.
Artifact Share allows teams to share AI doc artifacts via a persistent URL, gather human feedback, and update the document directly with coding agents.

The ad presents a clear workflow tailored to agent-assisted development teams. Visual transitions and text hierarchy are mostly readable, though metric roll animations look slightly artificial. Pacing and CTA hold times are effective for feed viewing.

p: ["text-only hook lacks visual stopping power for a scroll-stop moment","ghosted/overlapping text in frames 2-3 reads as a rendering glitch on first glance","small grayscale thumbnail in frame 3 looks like a blurred/corrupted asset, undermining artifact_score","narrative (spec doc -> comment -> AI edit) requires reading dense text across multiple frames to parse"]

The reading-order hook (wrote checkout-spec.html -> Who) is legible but quiet — it relies on curiosity from small text rather than a strong visual pattern-interrupt, so it may not stop a fast scroll. The middle frames do execute the intended message (human comment 'Give me the 3-week cut' -> numbers update 6wk/$38k to 3wk/$19k) and keep the artifactshare.com URL persistently on screen, which is good for product salience and clarity. However the diff-style ghosted overlay text and the odd blurred thumbnail in frame 3 read as visual noise/artifacts rather than intentional UI, and the CTA only lands in the final frame, so overall this is a solid-concept, mid-tier execution rather than a high-confidence performer.
